messages:
Ibrahim (support): VelvetApp reporting intermittent p95 spikes this morning and some 429s hitting their Dedicated pool. They say autoscale did not add capacity. Dropping notes + logs here.
Lina Patel: Which pool/node/tenant? Can you paste the node MIG layout? :mag:
Ibrahim (support): pool=eu-west-dedicated-3, node=drv-eu3-12, tenant=velvetapp-prod. MIG layout: sliceA=1g_5GB, sliceB=2g_10GB. Customer says spikes line up with a cron at 08:30 UTC.
Jamie - SRE: Oncall flagged drv-eu3-12 at ~08:30. Queue depth jumped; pods were pending but cluster autoscaler didn't treat them as scaleable because the node selector for new nodes didn't match annotations.
Max Chen: Important: were the 429s generated by our gateway (rate-limiter) or by an upstream auth check? That changes mitigation.
Ibrahim (support): 429s came back from our gateway while token verification was still processing. Client retries amplified their load. Sample from our logs:
```
2026-03-11T08:29:58Z velvetapp-prod req=xyz001 model=redwood-8b tokens=512 p95=380ms status=200
2026-03-11T08:30:22Z velvetapp-prod req=xyz002 model=redwood-8b tokens=512 p95=6100ms status=429 gateway_rate_limit
```
Ibrahim (support): They claim their normal traffic is ~6 qps single-shot, not a bulk job. So likely another tenant's scheduled batch overlapped.
Anya (runtime): Runtime metrics show SM_UTIL on the 2g slice hitting 96-99% and L3 eviction rates climbing. NVLink bandwidth looked healthy. Looks like a heavy batched scoring job on the sibling slice causing cache thrash.
Jamie - SRE: Confirmed. Node-level traces show long kernel queues on sliceB. No thermals or OOMs in dmesg. NVML snapshot stored in /var/log/rdw/collect-176900.
Max Chen: Scheduler/autoscaler findings?
Anya (runtime): Autoscaler scale-up path used node.labels.gpuType to pick nodes but ignored node.annotation.migAffinity. Because affinity is currently non-mandatory, the scale decision put new pods on drv-eu3-12 where sibling load existed. There's a known race where non-binding affinity allows packing on already hot slices.
Jamie - SRE: Short-term mitigations proposed:
- Move velvetapp-prod to an isolated dedicated pool (eu-west-dedicated-iso-2) — cordon + drain, ~3 minutes
- Temporarily bump min_nodes for eu-west-dedicated-3 to reduce immediate packing churn
- Add a per-tenant MIG taint+toleration for velvetapp to avoid sibling co-location
Ibrahim (support): Customer asked if migration can happen now — they're OK with a brief window.
Anya (runtime): I'll push a scheduler change to make migAffinity respected during scale-up (canary to eng-runtime). Also adding a runtime cap: runtime.max_concurrent_streams_per_slice=12 to limit simultaneous streams per slice.
Max Chen: Also recommend a circuit: route velvetapp to a lower-cost, verified variant (redwood-4b-quant) when p95 > 2s to avoid gateway backpressure and 429 amplification.
Jamie - SRE: I'll execute the migration once Anya's affinity update lands (ETA ~25m). I'll also raise min_nodes for eu-west-dedicated-3.
autoscaler-bot: [INFO] Action taken: min_nodes for pool eu-west-dedicated-3 increased from 2 -> 3 at 2026-03-11T08:45:12Z per SRE.
Ibrahim (support): Recording repro steps for eng:
1) On a test host with MIG layout (1g/2g) start a heavy batch generator: `wrk -t4 -c60 -d300s --script=batch-gen.lua http://internal-node:8080/batch`
2) From a separate tenant, run 5 qps single-shot generator: `rcli gen --model redwood-8b --qps 5 --tokens 512 --duration 300s`
3) Watch nvml and runtime p95; p95 expected to go >2s when batch saturates SM.
Ibrahim (support): Added customer traces and IDs to ticket TICKET-91234 and pointed out cron job overlap with another tenant's schedule.
Anya (runtime): Long-term fix: scheduler should treat migAffinity as hard preference during scale decisions and we should add noisy-job detection to quarantine heavy batch jobs (limit per-slice SM share). I'll open PR RDW-13021.
Jamie - SRE: I'll draft a runbook for rapid tenant-migration and autoscaler knobs — RDW-13022.
Max Chen: I'll own gateway retry/backoff updates and noisy-job detection design doc — RDW-13023. Also add a fallback routing rule for p95-based model downgrades.
Ibrahim (support): Updated TICKET-91234 with timeline and linked RDW tasks. Customer notified; they will accept temporary fallback model during migration.
Lina Patel: Update from customer: migration completed, p95 stabilized to ~420ms, no further 429s after move + fallback. They requested a full RCA when available.
Anya (runtime): Confirming post-migration traces show sibling batch caused KV cache churn leading to kernel queuing on sliceB. Will include NVML charts and cache eviction graphs in the postmortem.
Jamie - SRE: Closing this thread here; will add incident notes to tracker and follow up in PM. :white_check_mark:
